sentences.text: Shri Anil Upadhyay - Panel Lawyer for State.
Heard on the question of admission.
The appeal bearing arguable is admitted for final hearing.

Also heard on I.A. No.17048 of 2025,
which is first application under Section 430(1) of the BNSS, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant - Hukum Singh Yadav.
This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 27.12.2021 passed by the learned Special Judge,
POCSO, Panna in Special Case No.80 of 2021, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 363, 366A, 376(2)(N) and 323 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for three years and fine of Rs.1,000/-, R.I. for five years and fine of Rs.1,000/-, R.I. for ten years and fine of Rs.10,000/- and R.I. for three months and fine of Rs.500/- respectively, with default stipulations.

However, no separate sentence has been awarded for conviction under Section 5L,
J(ii)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has undergone actual custody of seven years, one month, and twenty-seven days, as per the custody report dated 22.08.2025.
It is further submitted that the FIR in the present case was lodged after an inordinate delay of one year, for which no plausible or satisfactory explanation has been given by the prosecution.
It is also submitted 2 CRA-132-2022 that there is no cogent or reliable evidence on record to establish the age of the prosecutrix.
Since the present appellant has served out more than half of the sentence awarded to him, the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed in favour of the appellant.
It is further submitted that there is no likelihood of early hearing of the instant appeal in near future.
The appellant is ready to abide by all the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
In view of the aforesaid, it is prayed that the sentence imposed on the appellant be suspended and he be released on bail.
Per contra , learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the application.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it is observed that the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(N) of the IPC, which prescribes a minimum sentence of ten years' rigorous imprisonment.
